h1: The Royal City Hotel Bangkok — the top 4-star pick for travellers connecting at the Southern Bus Terminal
intro: If you have an early-morning bus heading south — to Hua Hin, Krabi, Phuket, or Kanchanaburi — or you have just arrived in Bangkok late at night after a long-distance bus ride, the hotel you want is one that is on the same side of the city as the bus terminal, not across town in rush-hour traffic. The Royal City Hotel Bangkok is a 4-star hotel on Borommaratchachonnani Road, Bang Bumru, Bang Phlat, approximately 6 km from the Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai), around 10–15 minutes by Grab or taxi (no hotel shuttle — you call Grab yourself) · the hotel has 401 rooms, an outdoor pool, a fitness centre, 3 restaurants, free parking, and a variety of room types suited to couples and families alike · prices start from about ฿1,100/night in low season, with an average score of roughly 7.6 from over 360 reviews across multiple platforms.

body.html: Who this hotel is for — The Royal City Hotel Bangkok is built for people who are passing through western Thonburi, not for those using Bangkok as a sightseeing base · if your plan is to catch a bus from the Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai, on Borommaratchachonnani Road, Taling Chan) to Hua Hin, Krabi, Phuket, or Kanchanaburi, and you want to sleep close by without crossing the whole city at dawn — this is the clear number-one option in this zone · the hotel sits on the same road as the terminal, just 6 km apart, roughly 10–15 minutes by Grab, costing around 60–100 baht · the route is direct, no bridges or complicated turns, and there is minimal traffic on this stretch late at night or in the early morning, which is precisely when southbound-bus travellers need it · one thing to state plainly upfront: there is no hotel shuttle to or from the bus terminal — you call your own Grab or taxi every time.

Location and the surrounding area — the hotel stands at 800 Borommaratchachonnani Road, Bang Bumru, Bang Phlat, in the western Thonburi side of Bangkok · this is not a tourist district in the classic sense — there is no night market, no Grand Palace to walk to · what you do have is Central Pinklao shopping mall about 2 km away (5–7 minutes by car), with restaurants, a supermarket, and everything a traveller might need to stock up before a long bus journey · there are also 7-Elevens and street-food stalls a short walk from the hotel, handy for a late-night snack · for the main tourist sights on the Phra Nakhon side — Wat Phra Kaew, Khao San Road — plan on 15–25 minutes by Grab (8–12 km) · the nearest metro station, MRT Bang Yi Khan, is about 2.1 km away and would require a Grab connection · to put it simply: this hotel rewards people with their own car (free parking) or people happy to use Grab for every trip — it is not a "walk to everywhere" location.

"Very spacious room with a view — breakfast had a choice selection of Western and Thai dishes. Staff were incredibly helpful. Grab to Sai Tai Mai was only 10 minutes. Great value for the facilities you get."

Room types and condition — The Royal City Hotel has 401 rooms spread across a high-rise building in several tiers · the entry level is the Superior Modern Room, available as Twin (2 single beds) or Double (1 king bed) · a step up is the Deluxe Modern Room, running about 30 sqm, positioned from the 18th floor upward, with better city views and a fresher feel · there are Triple Rooms for families of three, and suites for those wanting extra space · the hotel completed a renovation in 2022, bringing a contemporary-modern style to the refurbished rooms: flat-screen TV, air conditioning, fridge, Wi-Fi, and an en-suite bathroom with complimentary toiletries in every room · what real reviews consistently say: spacious rooms and comfortable beds are the most reliably praised features, especially in the Deluxe category · the point that needs honest mention is that, because the building has age and 401 rooms is a lot, room condition is not uniform across every room — reviewers have flagged musty odours, dated furniture, and uneven cleaning in some rooms that were not part of the renovation scope · the simple fix: book a Deluxe Modern Room on the 18th floor or above, or specify a recently refurbished room when booking — it makes a noticeable difference.

Facilities and the pool — the reason The Royal City Hotel holds the top spot for this zone is the strength of its facilities relative to its price · it has an outdoor pool (and a children's pool), a fitness centre, a business centre, meeting rooms, and — crucially — free parking, which is genuinely hard to find at a 4-star property in Bangkok · free Wi-Fi covers the whole property · for food there are 3 on-site restaurants, including an all-day dining operation that runs a breakfast buffet praised in reviews for having both Thai and Western options — useful for travellers who need to eat before an early bus · the hotel also has a bar and lounge, a karaoke room, and laundry service · during the periods when the hotel takes in tour groups or conference guests, the common areas can feel busy; if you want quiet, choose a high floor and avoid peak check-in hours · overall, for the nightly rate, the amount of facilities on offer is hard to beat in this part of Bangkok.

Service — service is consistently a strength at The Royal City Hotel and is the category that scores highest in the data: Trip.com guests give service an 8.9 · reviewers repeatedly describe staff as friendly, approachable, and willing to help, with English communication at a workable level · there are honest caveats too: a handful of TripAdvisor reviews mention inconsistent housekeeping — some guests found their bathroom had not been cleaned during a multi-night stay · if you encounter this, the advice from reviewers is to flag it to the front desk, where staff typically respond promptly · check-in during busy periods may involve a short wait · overall, service sits comfortably at the standard expected from a value-focused 4-star hotel — attentive and friendly, not white-glove luxury.

What real guests say — both the praise and the gripes — pulling together reviews from Trip.com (score 8.4/42 reviews), HotelsCombined (6.8/161), TripAdvisor (3.2/5 from 155), and other aggregators, a consistent picture emerges · What guests praise most: spacious rooms and comfortable beds, the breakfast buffet's variety ("choice selection of western and Thai dishes"), friendly staff, the outdoor pool, free parking, reliable Wi-Fi, good city views from upper floors, and the value for money relative to facilities · What guests flag as issues: musty smells or dated elements in some rooms ("the room has a smell"), uneven cleaning standards between rooms, Wi-Fi that can be slow on lower floors, tour groups making the lobby busy at peak times, and — most importantly for tourist-minded travellers — a location that requires a Grab for every outing · the clearest pattern in the reviews is that guests who book this hotel knowing it is a transit base near the bus terminal tend to leave satisfied; guests expecting a sightseeing-central Bangkok hotel sometimes feel let down by the location.

"Older hotel but everything in pretty good condition — the facilities are better than I expected for the price. Staff spoke enough English, sorted out my early check-in without any fuss. Would use again as a stopover before the southern bus."

Pricing and value — the Superior Modern Room starts at roughly ฿1,100–1,500/night (approximately $33–45) in low season, climbing to around ฿1,800–2,500 during high season or long weekends · the Deluxe Modern Room, from the 18th floor, typically starts at about ฿1,600–2,000 in quieter periods · within the zone around Sai Tai Mai — the closest 4-star hotel with a pool, fitness centre, and free parking — this price represents strong value · the trade-off, as noted throughout, is the age of some rooms and the non-tourist location · if you are staying here specifically to connect with a southbound bus and need nothing more than a comfortable night, a proper breakfast, and a pool to relax by the evening before — every baht you spend here pays back well.

Good to know before you book — a few things that will make your stay noticeably smoother · first, there is no shuttle between the hotel and the Southern Bus Terminal — you need Grab or a metered taxi; the route is easy, 10–15 minutes, roughly 60–100 baht · second, if room condition matters to you, go for the Deluxe Modern Room on the 18th floor or above, or note in your booking request that you want a recently refurbished room · third, this hotel is great for drivers — free parking is included and the road access is simple · fourth, Central Pinklao shopping centre is 2 km away and 5–7 minutes by car, covering all practical needs from supermarket to pharmacy to restaurants · fifth, pick free cancellation when you book if your bus or travel plans might shift — ticket dates on southern routes can change.

The bottom line — from the full body of real reviews, The Royal City Hotel Bangkok is the strongest option in this zone for travellers transiting through the Southern Bus Terminal · it is not a flashy city-centre hotel, but it is a large 4-star property on the same road as the terminal, a short Grab away, with a pool, free parking, three restaurants, and a breakfast buffet — all at a price point that makes it hard to beat in western Thonburi · the trade-offs are rooms that vary in freshness across the property and a location that needs a car or Grab for everything · if you are after a walking-distance sightseeing hotel, look elsewhere · but if you need a solid, comfortable night close to Sai Tai Mai before an early-morning bus to Hua Hin, Krabi, Phuket, or Kanchanaburi — The Royal City Hotel Bangkok is the best answer in the neighbourhood.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Royal City Hotel Bangkok

faq.q: How far is The Royal City Hotel Bangkok from the Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai)?
faq.a: The hotel sits on Borommaratchachonnani Road — the same road as the terminal — approximately 6 km away, which takes about 10–15 minutes by Grab or taxi, costing roughly 60–100 baht · there is no hotel shuttle; you call Grab yourself · the route is direct with minimal traffic in the early morning or late at night.

faq.q: How much does The Royal City Hotel Bangkok cost? What room types are available?
faq.a: Prices start at roughly ฿1,100–1,500/night for a Superior Modern Room in low season · the Deluxe Modern Room (floor 18+, ~30 sqm) starts at around ฿1,600 · during high season or long weekends, rates climb to about ฿1,800–2,500 · there are also Triple Rooms for families and suites for those who need more space.

faq.q: Does The Royal City Hotel Bangkok have a pool and free parking?
faq.a: Yes to both · the hotel has an outdoor pool (plus a children's pool) and a fitness centre · free parking is included — a genuine rarity for a 4-star Bangkok hotel · there are also 3 on-site restaurants, a breakfast buffet, a bar and lounge, a business centre, and meeting rooms.

faq.q: Who is The Royal City Hotel Bangkok best for?
faq.a: It is the best option for travellers catching a bus from the Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai) to Hua Hin, Krabi, Phuket, Kanchanaburi, or other western/southern destinations, and for anyone wanting to overnight nearby on arrival · it is also excellent for guests with a car (free parking) and for families who want space and facilities at a fair price · it is not ideal for people who want to walk to Bangkok's main sights.

faq.q: Are the rooms at The Royal City Hotel in good condition?
faq.a: The hotel renovated in 2022 but condition is not uniform across all 401 rooms · some rooms are fresh and well-maintained; others still show the building's age with musty smells or dated furniture · to get the best experience, book a Deluxe Modern Room on floor 18 or above, or request a recently refurbished room when you make your reservation.

faq.q: How do you get from The Royal City Hotel to Central Pinklao and Khao San Road?
faq.a: Central Pinklao is about 2 km away, 5–7 minutes by car or Grab · Khao San Road is about 8 km away, roughly 15–20 minutes by Grab depending on traffic · there is no BTS or MRT within walking distance — the nearest station, MRT Bang Yi Khan, is about 2.1 km away and requires a Grab connection.
